title: The modal collects the schedule, then optional last-service dates
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in, on the build under test, as a service advisor with the view customers and create and edit customers permissions.
  2. Your user also holds "Settings Service" to seed the schedules.
  3. Three schedules (standard seeding steps): "Fleet PM" with service "pm-a" (Every 3 months); "Yard PM" with service "PM-A" (Every 3 months); "Highway Tractor PM" with PM-A (Every 3 months), PM-B (Every 6 months) and PM-C (Every 12 months).
  4. Asset 402 enrolled on "Fleet PM" and "Yard PM". On its Maintenance tab: the "pm-a" row menu > Mark complete > Completed elsewhere, Reset date 1 Aug 2026 > confirm; the "PM-A" row (Yard PM) > Mark complete > Completed elsewhere, Reset date 1 Sep 2026 > confirm.
custom_steps:
1. On asset 402 click Enroll in Schedule and read the modal title (the design titles it "Enroll in a schedule") and the line beneath it; open the same modal on another asset and compare the title.
  2. Pick "Highway Tractor PM" and read what the modal asks for, in order, and how "(optional)" is shown.
  3. Read the pre-filled last service dates of PM-A, PM-B and PM-C.
  4. Read what the modal says about a blank date; try to enter a date after today for PM-B.
  5. Leave PM-B and PM-C blank and click Enroll; read the three due dates on the Maintenance tab.
  6. Read asset 402's Maintenance tab.
  7. Hover the (i) beside the "LAST SERVICE (OPTIONAL)" heading.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • The title is the same for every asset (static); the unit and customer appear in the body at normal weight (e.g. "402 · 2019 Freightliner Cascadia · Aacrest Works").
  • The modal asks for the schedule, then one last service date per service, each with "(optional)" in brackets beside its label; it asks for no readings.
  • PM-A is pre-filled with 1 Sep 2026: "pm-a" and "PM-A" both match despite the capitals, and the later completion (1 Sep over 1 Aug) wins. PM-B and PM-C are blank.
  • The modal states that a blank date counts from today; a date after today cannot be entered.
  • PM-A comes due Dec 2026 (1 Sep 2026 + 3 months); PM-B comes due 6 months from today and PM-C 12 months from today.
  • Every service of "Highway Tractor PM" was added (none skipped), and PM-A appears on separate rows for "Yard PM" and "Highway Tractor PM": overlapping services on two schedules are allowed.
  • On the design the (i) reads "One last-service date per service. Brakes done last week and an oil service long overdue cannot be described by a single date. Left blank, counting starts today."

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-3780, story SV-10564 (S7, Enrol an asset onto a schedule), Chunk 1 MR (Confluence 886931488) as edited 5 October 2026, S7 (Choosing the schedule, then the services; S7-R2, S7-R4, S7-R7, S7-R8, S7-E3); Design board "Chunk 1.dc.html" (MR V2 Claude Design project, version of 6 October 2026), artboard X1; read 6 Oct 2026. Source-verified 6 October 2026; not yet build-verified.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S7-R7: “The modal title will be static. The unit and customer belong in the body at normal content weight”
  • S7-R2: “The modal will collect, in order: the schedule, then one optional last service date per service. Current readings are not collected here”
  • S7-R4: “Each last service date is filled in with the most recent completion on this asset of a service with the same name, from any schedule”
  • S7-R4: “Names match ignoring capitals and surrounding spaces. Where two services match, the latest completion wins”
  • S7-R4: “Blank means counting starts today, stated in the modal. The date cannot be in the future”
  • S7-R8: “(optional) will sit in brackets inline with its label”
  • S7-E3: “A due date comes from a last service date the advisor entered or the system recorded, otherwise from today”
  • Design board, artboard X1: “Left blank, counting starts today.”
  • S7-E5: “Enrolment applies the schedule as it stands. Nothing is skipped or negotiated”
  • S7-E4: “An asset may be enrolled on more than one schedule. Overlapping services are allowed and produce separate rows”
  • Design board, artboard X1 (title): “Enroll in a schedule”
  • Design board, artboard X1 (LAST SERVICE (i)): “One last-service date per service. Brakes done last week and an oil service long overdue cannot be described by a single date. Left blank, counting starts today.”
